chunks: He said: Abul Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni, may Allah have mercy on him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha', from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his progeny, said:
"When Allah wishes well for a servant, He makes him learned in the religion."
And may Allah bless our master Muhammad the Prophet and his family, and grant them peace.

key_terms.الدين: The religion -- referring to Islam in its totality
key_terms.فقهه: He gives him deep understanding (tafaqquh) -- comprehensive religious insight, not merely jurisprudence

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about Allah wishing good for someone?
ai.summary: This prophetic hadith, transmitted through Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq from the Prophet, establishes that deep understanding of religion (fiqh) is a sign of divine favor. The word 'faqaha' here means comprehensive understanding, not just jurisprudence. This hadith is widely narrated in both Sunni and Shia collections and has been foundational in Islamic educational tradition.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 9. He said: Abul Qasim Ja’far ibn Muhammad - may Allah have mercy on him, reported to me from Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn Ya’qoob al-Kulayni - may Allah bless him with mercy, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn ‘Ali al-Washha’, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who reported from Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, said:
"When Allah wishes well for a servant, He makes him learned in the Religion (i.e. Islam)."
And may Allah bless our master, Muhammad and his progeny.
